 Learn more Take-Two Interactive Chairman & CEO Strauss Zelnick says artificial intelligence will transform the video game industry, but he doesn't believe It will lead to fewer jobs. He says technology ultimately needs to serve one goal: make great entertainment. Zelnick sits down with David Rubenstein on this week's episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations. This interview was recorded October 19 in New York. 
 Video Transcript 00:00 Speaker A How is AI affecting your industry? Do you use AI to make any video games and is AI going to employ more people in your industry or unemploy more people in your industry. 
 00:13 Speaker B So the video game business has used artificial intelligence and machine learning from the very beginning. We've always been leaders in the space. Um, it's kind of a a mixed term on consumers of video games now because the perception is that if you use AI, it won't be any good. Um, so I tend to use the word technology, but the the leaps forward in technology are are pretty astonishing and I do think they'll influence pretty much everything we do, but again, at the end of the day, our job is to make hits. We use technology in the service of making hits. We don't use, we don't make entertainment so that we can excel in technology. 
 01:04 Speaker A But in in the world now we're operating people, some people are saying that AI will unemploy people in your industry. You think that'll happen or not? 
 01:13 Speaker B Absolutely not. There is zero evidence that technology reduces employment. To the contrary, great technology drives productivity, you know this better than I, productivity drives GDP, GDP drives employment. AI has been commercialized for three years. We know the billions of dollars in revenue that Anthropic and Open AI already generate. What's the unemployment rate in the US today, little over 4%. What was it three years ago, a little over 4%.
